name: Vouch
long_description:
Vouch is the new-age wealth manager for India’s young and ambitious professionals, with no minimums. India’s wealth industry is antiquated: great help starts at Rs 5 crore, and everyone else is left with a local agent or a trading app. Vouch’s AI agents, trained by experienced wealth managers, are filling the void: they plan your money, act on it once you approve, and keep it on track.

Indians are getting wealthier and moving that wealth into markets: $2.37 trillion in new financial wealth by 2030, and stocks and mutual funds up from 2% to 15% of household savings since 2012. At Vouch, we're starting with mutual funds before growing into the one place this burgeoning, new India manages its money.

launches.title: Vouch - India's personal wealth manager
launches.tagline: Expert-trained AI wealth agents, built for India's 100M+ professionals
launches.body:
I'm [Arnav Ghatiwala](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arnav-ghatiwala/), founder of [Vouch](http://vouchwealth.com/).

**TL;DR: Vouch is a personal wealth manager for India's 100M+ professionals. It understands your money and goals, builds your plan, makes the moves, and keeps watch.**

<https://youtu.be/gWd4FVlxOMo>

### **Why I'm building this**

My first job, at 16, was at a wealth management firm in India. I saw up close what great advice does for a family's wealth, and how few families in India ever get it. I went on to study Computer Science at Penn, worked at Jane Street, and became the youngest PM at Robinhood to launch a product: the Advisor Network, which helped bring wealth management to more people.

Now I'm back home, building a wealth manager for the new India.

### **The problem**

A new generation of Indians is earning more than ever and wants to make the most of it. But the wealth industry was built for the old India. Great quality help comes with Rs 5 crore+ (\~$570K) minimums, which equates to <1% of the population.

Everyone else gets a neighbourhood mutual fund agent or a DIY trading app.

### **What Vouch does**

Vouch handles your money end to end. Connect the investments you already hold, tell us your goals, and Vouch:

* **Understands your money:** reviews every holding across your family, and spots overlapping funds, high fees and gaps
* **Builds your plan:** a clear, tax-aware plan for what you're saving towards
* **Makes the moves:** switches funds, rebalances and sets up SIPs (monthly investments) at the lowest tax cost, once you say yes
* **Keeps watch:** finds forgotten investments and unclaimed money, uses your tax-free gains every year, harvests losses before the tax year ends, and flags anything that needs you

Under the hood, our agents are trained against evals set by veteran wealth managers, so they make the same calls an expert would, for every portfolio.

We're starting with mutual funds, then expanding to every asset class, and later to your cash flow: income, spending and saving. Vouch is currently a licensed mutual fund distributor, empanelled with 27+ fund houses, and we’re swtiching to fiduciary advice - an RIA (fee-based adviser) registration is underway.

### **Where we're going: Wealthfront's start, Vanguard's endgame**

Wealthfront proved software can manage money for millions of people. But it sits downstream: a small fee on funds someone else makes, in a market where every competitor races that fee to zero.

Vanguard owns the products. That's where the durable economics are.

We're starting where Wealthfront did, as the relationship people trust with their money. The goal is to own upstream managed products too, so we aren't the ones getting price compressed.

### **How you can help**

* **If you're an Indian professional, or your money is in India:** get early access at [**vouchwealth.com**](http://vouchwealth.com) and I'll onboard you personally.
* **If you run a company with a team in India:** Vouch could be a perk for your employees. I'd love to talk.
* **Intros to Indian professionals.** Friends, family, your network. Point them to [**vouchwealth.com**](http://vouchwealth.com), or send them my way.

Thanks, YC!
